blocks.title: Safe lifting, squats, hinges and pushes
Pulls, single legs, carries and skills

summary.title: Bracing, breathing, lifting safely
points: Brace before every rep: tighten all around the midsection; don't suck the belly in.
Breathe in before the hard part, out through it.
Brief breath holds raise blood pressure; avoid them with high blood pressure or heart conditions.
Pick weights up with the bell close, hips back, flat back, then drive through the feet.
Use the range you control; joint pain means stop and change the exercise.

exercises.scenario: You're about to deadlift a 16 kg bell from the floor.

questions.prompt: Which set-up is right?
options: Bell beside one foot, lift with one arm and twist
Hold your breath for the whole set of ten
Bell a stride in front, legs straight, reach down with a rounded back
Bell between the feet, hips back, flat back, brace

questions.prompt: When do you breathe out on most reps?
options: During the easy lowering phase only, then hold the breath while pushing
Through the hard part of the lift

exercises.scenario: A colleague with high blood pressure wants to start lifting.

questions.prompt: What breathing advice fits?
options: Breathing doesn't matter for strength training
Breathe out through the effort and avoid long breath holds; check with a doctor
Hold the breath on every rep to brace harder
questions.explanation: Breath holds raise blood pressure briefly, sometimes a lot.

questions.prompt: What does bracing mean?
options: Sucking the belly button in as far as possible

summary.title: Squat family
points: Goblet squat: elbows down between the knees, sit between the heels, knees follow toes.
Split squat: long stance, back knee straight down, push through the front foot.
Bulgarian split squat: rear foot on a chair; front foot far enough forward.
Split squats make light weights harder: one leg does most of the work.
Easier: squat to a chair. Harder: more load, slower lowering, pauses.

exercises.scenario: Your heels lift at the bottom of the goblet squat.

questions.prompt: What's the first fix?
options: Go heavier so the bell pulls you back down into the heels
Sit between the heels, keeping the weight over mid-foot
Lock the knees at the top harder

questions.prompt: You've outgrown 12 kg goblet squats and have only 10 kg dumbbells. What next?
options: Stop training legs until you buy more
More goblet squat reps at 12 kg, up to 60 per set
questions.explanation: One leg carries most of the load.

exercises.scenario: In your Bulgarian split squat the front knee shoots far past the toes and the heel lifts.

questions.prompt: What's likely wrong?
options: The front foot is too close to the chair
The chair is too low for a beginner to use safely
questions.explanation: Step the front foot further out.

questions.prompt: Which is an easier version of the split squat?
options: Rear foot raised on a chair, with dumbbells
Pausing at the bottom with heavier weights

summary.title: Hinge family
points: Deadlift teaches the shape: hips back, flat back, push the floor away.
Romanian deadlift: soft knees, slide down the thighs until the hamstrings stretch.
Swing: hike, snap the hips, bell floats to chest height; arms are ropes.
Learn deadlift, then RDL, then swing.
Kettlebell evidence is limited; treat swings as useful, not magic.

exercises.scenario: During swings your shoulders burn and the bell feels heavy at the top.

questions.prompt: What's likely wrong?
options: You're breathing out at the top
You're snapping the hips too hard
The bell is too light, so you have to work harder with the arms
questions.explanation: The hips launch the bell; arms guide it.

questions.prompt: How low should an RDL go?
options: As low as possible, touching the floor with the weights even if the back rounds
Until the hamstrings stretch with a flat back
questions.explanation: Range is set by the hamstrings and a flat back.

exercises.scenario: A friend wants to start with swings on day one.

questions.prompt: What order do you suggest?
options: Swing first, since it's the most important hinge to master
questions.explanation: Learn the shape, then the stretch, then speed.

questions.prompt: What does the evidence on kettlebells say?
options: It proves kettlebells beat all other strength training

summary.title: Push family
points: Push-ups are a full chest, shoulder and triceps exercise.
Matched to effort, push-ups built similar muscle and strength to a light bench press in 8 weeks.
Push-up: straight body, elbows about 45°, chest to a fist from the floor.
Floor press: elbows touch the floor lightly; no bench needed.
Overhead press: brace, press beside the ear, don't lean back.

exercises.scenario: You can do 30 push-ups.

questions.prompt: How do you keep progressing?
options: Stop doing push-ups and only stretch
Do sets of 60 to failure every session
questions.explanation: Feet raised, slow lowering, pauses or a band.

questions.prompt: Which is an easier push-up?
options: Feet raised on a chair, with a pause at the bottom
Hands on a bench or wall

exercises.scenario: A friend says push-ups are 'just a warm-up'.

questions.prompt: What did the 2017 study find?
options: Similar muscle and strength gains to a matched light bench press
Push-ups built no muscle at all compared with the bench
Push-ups beat a heavy bench press

questions.prompt: What's the main fault in the overhead press?
options: Leaning back to finish the rep
Pressing the weight straight up beside the ear

summary.title: Pull family
points: One-arm row: hand on a chair, pull the elbow to the hip, shoulders square.
Renegade row: row from a plank without the hips twisting.
Band pulldown: kneel, band anchored high, elbows to the ribs.
Band pull-aparts train rear shoulders and upper back.
Row in every session; no bar needed.

exercises.scenario: Your torso twists as you row the dumbbell.

questions.prompt: What does it suggest?
options: Too heavy, or the brace is lost
Rows should twist for full range
Too light, so you need to twist to make it harder

questions.prompt: Which exercise covers the vertical pull without a bar?
options: Renegade row in a wide stance

exercises.scenario: You want a quick upper-back exercise for the warm-up.

questions.prompt: Which fits?
options: Heavy one-arm rows to near failure

questions.prompt: What does the renegade row add over a normal row?
options: A heavier load than any other pulling exercise

summary.title: Lunges, step-ups, carries
points: Reverse lunge: step back, knee down, push through the front foot.
Step-up: drive through the top foot; don't push off the floor leg.
Farmer's carry: heavy weight in each hand, tall, short steps, 20–40 m.
Suitcase carry: one hand only; the trunk resists leaning.
Single-leg work and carries carry over to sport.

exercises.scenario: On step-ups you bounce off the floor leg to get up.

questions.prompt: What's the fix?
options: Drive through the top foot only
Use a higher step so the bounce is no longer possible
questions.explanation: The top leg should do the work.

questions.prompt: How far do you carry in a farmer's carry?
options: As far as you can walk in ten minutes
One step, then put the weights down to rest

exercises.scenario: You want a simple core exercise using your heaviest bell.

questions.prompt: Which carry fits best?
options: Farmer's carry with two light bells held at the chest
questions.explanation: One-sided load makes the trunk resist leaning.

questions.prompt: Why put carries at the end of a session?
options: They need the most technique, so you do them when fresh
Simple, safe, and uses your heaviest kit

summary.title: Full-body kettlebell skills
points: Get-up: eyes on the bell, arm locked, one step at a time; practise light.
Clean: hike, snap, elbow back, bell rolls into the rack at the chest.
Snatch: learn after swings and cleans; punch through to lock out overhead.
Rack position: bell on the forearm, wrist straight, elbow tucked.
Benefits beyond variety and conditioning are not well proven.

exercises.scenario: The bell bangs your forearm at the top of each clean.

questions.prompt: What's the fix?
options: Elbow back, bell close, let it roll around the hand
Use a heavier bell so it moves slower
Grip the handle harder and curl the bell up to the chest
questions.explanation: A close path stops the flip.

questions.prompt: How often should a beginner practise the get-up?
options: Every day, heavy, at the end of each session
Once a week, light, at the start of a session

exercises.scenario: A friend wants to start kettlebells with snatches.

questions.prompt: What do you suggest?
options: Snatches first, because they're the best fat-burning exercise
Swings and cleans first; snatch later
questions.explanation: Build the hinge and the path first.

questions.prompt: Where does a clean end?
options: Overhead, with the arm locked out
questions.explanation: Bell on the forearm against the chest.

summary.title: Safe lifting, squats, hinges, pushes
points: Brace and breathe on every rep; pick up from the floor with hips back.
Squats: goblet first, then split squats to make light weights harder.
Hinges: deadlift, RDL, then swing; hips do the work.
Pushes: push-up versions, floor press, overhead press.
Progress the version, not just the reps.

exercises.scenario: You plan a lower-body pair and a push for session A with a 12 kg bell and 10 kg dumbbells.

questions.prompt: Which set fits best?
options: Goblet squat at 12 kg, a two-hand deadlift at 12 kg and wall push-ups
Split squat, single-leg RDL, feet-raised push-up
questions.explanation: One-sided and harder versions make light kit work.

questions.prompt: Your swing burns the shoulders. Which earlier exercise do you revisit?
options: The overhead press, to strengthen the shoulders first

questions.prompt: Explain how to pick a weight up safely from the floor.
questions.modelAnswer: Stand close with the bell between your feet, push the hips back and bend the knees with a flat back, brace, then stand by driving through the feet. Put it down the same way.

exercises.scenario: You can do 30 push-ups and 25 goblet squats at 12 kg.

questions.prompt: What's the next step for each?
options: Stop both and switch to cardio
Harder versions: feet-raised push-ups and split squats
More reps of the same: 50 push-ups and 40 squats
questions.explanation: Keep effort in the useful range.

questions.prompt: What does 'progress the version' mean?
options: Switch to a harder variation of the same pattern
Change to a completely different movement pattern each week

summary.title: Pulls, single legs, carries, skills
points: Rows every session; band pulldowns fill the vertical pull.
Lunges and step-ups train one leg and balance.
Carries train grip and trunk; suitcase carries add side-trunk work.
Get-ups and cleans are skills: learn them light.
Swap within the pattern when kit, level or joints require it.

exercises.scenario: Session B needs a pull, a lunge, a carry and a skill, all in 30 minutes.

questions.prompt: Which combination fits?
options: One-arm row, reverse lunge, suitcase carry, light get-up
Snatches, pull-ups, Bulgarian squats and overhead walks
questions.explanation: One per pattern, at your level.

questions.prompt: Where does the get-up go in the session?
options: At the very end, when you're most tired
At the start, as a slow skill

questions.prompt: Name a swap for each: no pull-up bar, wrist discomfort in push-ups, short on time.
questions.modelAnswer: No bar: rows plus band pulldowns. Wrist discomfort: floor press or push-ups on dumbbell handles. Short on time: replace two exercises with a set of swings.

exercises.scenario: Your plan says 'one hinge' and RDLs with 12 kg feel easy.

questions.prompt: Which swap keeps the pattern?
options: Goblet squat, since it also works the legs

questions.prompt: Which pair balances the upper body without a bar?

summary.title: The exercise library: the whole picture
points: Brace, breathe, and lift from the floor with hips back.
Each pattern has easier, main and harder exercises.
Light kit works with one-sided versions, slow lowering and harder variations.
Rows and bands cover pulling without a bar; carries finish sessions.
Kettlebell skills are learnt light; their extra benefits aren't well proven.
Keep the pattern, change the exercise.

exercises.scenario: You build a 30-minute full-body session with your current kit.

questions.prompt: Which set covers every main pattern?
options: Split squat, single-leg RDL, push-up, one-arm row, suitcase carry
Push-up, floor press, overhead press, curl, lateral raise
Goblet squat, swing, deadlift, Romanian deadlift and a step-up

questions.prompt: How do you set the weight for each?
options: Test sets with reps in reserve
Copy the starting load from the card regardless of feel
Use the heaviest weight you own for everything
questions.explanation: Starting loads on the cards are only a guide.

questions.prompt: One exercise hurts a joint. What do you do?
options: Push through the pain to finish the set
Drop the whole pattern for good
Stop it and swap within the pattern
questions.explanation: Joint pain means change the exercise.

exercises.scenario: Looking back at your old routine: same push-ups and goblet squats every week.

questions.prompt: What does Module 4 give you that was missing?
options: A single perfect exercise to repeat every session forever
A menu of exercises per pattern, with easier and harder versions

questions.prompt: Which skill should wait until swings and cleans are solid?
questions.explanation: Learn the hinge and path first.

questions.prompt: Write the exercise card fields from memory.
questions.modelAnswer: Pattern, main muscles, equipment, set-up, cues, common errors, easier / harder, starting load.
